name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that runs before any submission. It flags low-contrast elements in real time, forcing designers to fix them upfront. This guarantees every screen meets accessibility standards before we ship, cutting last-minute rework. The trade-off is a small performance hit during editing, but it saves far more time than fixing broken contrast later.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Blocking submissions risks training users to blame the system for their own contrast failures, not fixing the root cause. A live checker is better than nothing, but it’s a bandage—we should instead teach designers why contrast matters upfront, then let them iterate freely. The argument settles when we compare user behavior before and after: if designers still ignore warnings, the real fix is redesigning the workflow, not the tool.
